summary: You need 135 graduate units, including the six core courses (ENVRES 310, 315, 320, 330, 340 and 398) and 25 letter-graded units of research electives numbered 200 or above in your two areas of concentration. Your advisor checks the 3.0 GPA in all PhD courses, the B average in the research electives, and that at least 90 units were taken at Stanford, and the department records grant proposals, advisor meetings, annual reviews, teaching, the qualifying exam, candidacy, the oral exam and the dissertation. The PhD-to-MS section describes a change of degree and is not a PhD requirement.

freeform-text.why: The page's requirements text restates the rules already here: "In the first two years, complete the PhD core course sequence" (Core Courses), "Complete a minimum of 135 units for the PhD. At least 90 units must be taken at Stanford" and "Students must pass at least 25 letter-graded course units (200-level and above) with a B (3.0) average or higher" (Research Electives), and the grant proposal, quarterly advisor meeting and annual review rules. Nothing new to check.

V2uQ7GG6.why: "Complete a minimum of 135 units for the PhD. At least 90 units must be taken at Stanford ... The remaining units should come from coursework taken to fulfill the research electives needed in the student's two Areas of Concentration - 25 units of which must be letter-graded courses numbered 200 and above, and passed with a minimum B (3.0) average." The 135 total is on the program; which courses fit the areas of concentration is set with the co-advisors.
